title: Quiz: Binary Logic & Numbers - Fundamentals
prompt: Test your foundational understanding of binary numbers, hexadecimal, and basic logic operations.

questions.question: How is a positive integer negated using the two's complement representation?
options: By flipping the sign bit from 0 to 1.
By taking the one's complement (toggling all 0s to 1s and vice versa) and adding 1.
By shifting all bits to the left by one position.
By taking the one's complement and subtracting 1.
questions.explanation: Negating a number is done by taking the one's complement (toggling all 0s to 1s, and vice versa) and adding 1 to the result.
questions.hint: It is a two-step mathematical process, starting with flipping every single bit.

questions.question: How many bits are represented by a single hexadecimal digit?
questions.explanation: Each hexadecimal digit corresponds to a particular 4-bit pattern.
questions.hint: Hexadecimal is base-16. 2 to what power equals 16?

questions.question: What mathematical operation does a Logical Shift Left (LSL) instruction simulate?
options: Division by a power of two.
Multiplication by a power of two.
Sign extension of a negative number.
questions.explanation: LSL is a quick way to do multiplication by a power of two (i.e. by 2^n, where n is the shift count).
questions.hint: Shifting the binary digits to the left makes the number larger.

questions.question: Which ARMv8 instruction is used to perform a logical NOT operation?
questions.explanation: The NOT operation is implemented using mvn (move NOT).

questions.question: In signed integers, what does a 1 in the left-most bit indicate?
questions.explanation: All negative numbers will have a 1 in the left-most bit, called the sign bit.
questions.hint: This bit acts as a flag to indicate the polarity of the number.
